title: Administrators and shared accounts
feed: T7.1's evidence packs for A.5.16 and A.5.18
context: At GlobalConnect Manila the CRM runs on HelpLoop, named here only for context. AppAdmin is a brand-neutral simulator that shows the same governance information. All tenant data is synthetic.
atWork: At work, a junior analyst opens an application's admin console when an access review needs evidence: the extract shows who had access on one day, the console shows who holds it now and how they sign in.
owner: Your sprint rates the access controls from the Manila office's own account of them. Before the evidence packs for A.5.16 and A.5.18 are built, look at the CRM itself, as of the account extract of 16 November 2026: who holds Administrator and whether an approval stands behind it, who does not sign in through the Group's single sign-on, and which setting allows it. Capture what you find, so the packs can rely on it without anyone opening the console.
rules: Access is granted only with the approval of the asset owner. Shared and generic accounts are prohibited, except break-glass accounts that are registered, sealed and monitored. Single sign-on is used wherever an application supports it.
Access is requested by the line manager and approved by the asset owner, and the approval is kept. In force since 1 October 2026: a grant before that date has no approval to find.
Your ACC-RULES matrix sets what each role needs on the CRM. A role that holds more than its line says is more than the job needs.

parts.title: Administrators with no approval
parts.ask: Find every administrator who has no approval ticket, and capture exactly those accounts.
parts.where: Users & roles. Use two filters together: one for the role, one for the approval. Press Capture evidence, then choose the capture here.

parts.title: Does the job need Administrator?
parts.ask: For each administrator you captured, decide whether the job needs the Administrator role.
parts.where: Users & roles gives each account's Job. Your ACC-RULES matrix (Access Reviews › Privilege Check) says which role of the CRM each job gets.
options: The job needs it: it administers the CRM

parts.title: Accounts outside single sign-on
parts.ask: Find every account that does not sign in through single sign-on, and capture exactly those accounts.
parts.where: Users & roles. Clear your filters first. The column to filter is Sign-in method.

parts.title: The setting that allows it
parts.ask: Which tenant setting lets an account sign in without single sign-on? Search for it and capture that one row.
parts.where: Tenant settings. Type part of the setting's name in Search so that only its row is left.
